subject: Social Media
title: Deep Work Is Dying
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Deep Work Is Dying.

hook.text: Carl Jung built a stone tower with no electricity to think. Today, people can't write an email without checking X.

buildup.text: Cal Newport defines deep work as focused, undistracted effort on cognitively demanding tasks. It's increasingly rare.

discovery.text: Knowledge workers spend 60% of their day on shallow tasks: email, chat, notifications. Deep work gets the scraps.

twist.text: Deep work produces most of the value. A 4-hour focused session outperforms 8 hours of fragmented busyness.

climax.text: Social media trains the opposite skill: rapid scanning, shallow processing, quick reactions. The brain adapts to that.

punchline.text: Focus is a muscle. Scrolling atrophies it.

quiz.question: What does Cal Newport call focused, undistracted cognitive effort?
